To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3CR quasar host clusters have X-ray luminosities of ∼1044–1045 erg s−1 and that they are all cooling flows.
the 3CR quasar sample is associated with moderately rich clusters of galaxies.
the 3CR quasar host clusters are massive and have high X-ray luminosities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Are there any 3CR quasar hosts that are not in clusters?
the following questions: (i) Are powerful radio-loud quasars preferentially located in clusters of galaxies?
the detection of the host clusters of powerful quasars at redshifts out 0.73, and with the properties of the intracluster gas in these objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3CR quasar sample is drawn from clusters of galaxies with a median richness class of ∼1, with the more distant objects in richer environments than those closer to the observer.

the 3CR quasar sample is associated with moderately rich clusters, with a median mass of ∼2×1015 h−1M⊙ and a median cooling time of the order of 2 Gyr, and that a significant fraction (at least 50 per cent) of the quasar host clusters are cooling flows.
3CR quasar host clusters have a mean temperature of 4–5 keV and are moderately rich, with a mean richness parameter of 30–40.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

3CR radio galaxies and quasars are found in clusters of galaxies with masses in the range 1014–1015 M⊙, with the more distant ones in more massive systems, as expected from the observed radio-luminosity-velocity correlation for radio galaxies.

the 3CR quasar host clusters are not as rich and X-ray luminous as the host clusters of the more distant 3CRR quasars, but that the 3CRR and 3CR host clusters are similar in terms of their X-ray luminosities and cooling flows.
the 3CR quasar host clusters are not unusual in terms of their X-ray emission properties, but that the X-ray emission from the quasar itself is too faint for detection in most cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host clusters of 3CR quasar have properties that are typical of the general population of galaxy clusters.

the host clusters of powerful radio-loud quasars have similar properties to those of clusters of galaxies hosting less luminous radio sources, in agreement with the unified scheme of active galactic nucleus classification.

the 3CR sample of powerful radio galaxies and quasars is not representative of the parent population of active galactic nuclei, in the sense that it does not sample the full range of host cluster environments.
